units: milliseconds; percentages use paired batch means, not ratios of pooled medians
commands: nix develop .#integration --ignore-environment --keep TERM --command node packages/scenarios/benchmark/caller-capture.mjs .data/benchmarks/caller-capture-same e8a3dda1 same-process
execution: Browser runs were serialized through the host browser lock. No trace recording was started. Repository checks completed before measurements.

design.order: AB/BA alternating, 20 pairs of each order
design.perCall: performance.now before construction through execution and read assertions; click count checked outside timer
design.paired: Difference of batch mean on minus control; percent divides by control batch mean; share divides by on batch mean
design.interval: 10000 deterministic percentile bootstrap resamples of 40 whole pairs; medians; seed 283; exploratory intervals do not model serial dependence

limitations: Separate processes leave runtime, heap and browser frame-phase confounds. URL negative control and click order effects demonstrate this; retain as diagnostics, do not interpret differences as pure capture cost.

Same process uses original capture function bodies but changes const bindings to let and appends a benchmark setter. This may affect optimization; it is not byte-identical module code. Same page and browser remove cross-process state differences.
URL is a retained Watchable read with no caller capture; fresh title and count operations are constructed in each timed iteration.

fn-url is a synthetic public Operation.fn wrapper around the URL read. Definition capture is outside timing; invocation capture is inside. Other measured operations use named, not fn. Named cost includes captures of nested operations.
Click includes browser frame waits that may absorb CPU overhead. Failure to resolve overhead is not proof of zero CPU cost.
Single machine and runtime; no CPU affinity or frequency controls; serial batching and GC can affect variability.
